Title: Life Goals Collaborative Care for Patients With Bipolar Disorder and Cardiovascular Disease Risk

Title: Collaborative care for schizophrenic patients in primary care: A double blind, randomized clinical trial of efficacy and safety
Author: Saad Salman et al.
Comment: Group-specific analysed Ns are not stated in Table 3. Per the extraction rule, the Table 1 header Ns (39 usual care; 41 collaborative care) were used, but the paper reports multiple conflicting sample counts elsewhere (46/50 randomized, 46/46 compared, and 92 in Discussion). Title: Impact of Pharmacist–Psychiatrist Collaborative Patient Education on Medication Adherence and Quality of Life (QOL) of Bipolar Affective Disorder (BPAD) Patients
Author: Mishra et al.
Comment: The paper states that follow-ups occurred at nearly 1-month intervals but does not explicitly assign an elapsed month to the third follow-up. The third follow-up was selected as the latest reported assessment no later than 6 months. Analysed completer Ns (35 control, 38 test) were used. No effect size, t statistic, degrees of freedom, or mean difference was explicitly reported; these fields were left null.
Study Environment: Psychiatry outpatient department in a tertiary care setting
Medium: In-person pharmacist-provided education supported by patient information leaflets, alongside usual psychiatrist care
Topic of Content: Bipolar disorder, prescribed medications, medication adherence, and quality of life
interaction_type: Patient and carer education/counseling during follow-up visits
Outcome measurement: WHOQOL-BREF Domain 2: Psychological health at third follow-up
effect_direction: Positive values favour collaborative care (higher score indicates better quality of life).
